title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG136
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
journal: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, published 28 August 2019, last updated 26 February 2026
result: Step 1 treatment, recommendations marked 2019: offer a calcium channel blocker to adults starting step 1 antihypertensive treatment who are aged 55 or over and do not have type 2 diabetes, or who are of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin and do not have type 2 diabetes, of any age (1.4.35); if a calcium channel blocker is not tolerated, for example because of oedema, offer a thiazide-like diuretic (1.4.36); if there is evidence of heart failure, offer a thiazide-like diuretic (1.4.37). Step 2: if hypertension is not controlled on a calcium channel blocker, offer the choice of an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin receptor blocker or a thiazide-like diuretic in addition (1.4.42); if it is not controlled on an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker, offer the choice of a calcium channel blocker or a thiazide-like diuretic in addition (1.4.41). Step 3: offer an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker with a calcium channel blocker and a thiazide-like diuretic (1.4.45). Step 4: patients whose hypertension is not controlled on optimal tolerated doses of those three drugs are regarded as having resistant hypertension (1.4.46).
